turns.text: A hum climbs up through the grating before anything else registers, and it isn't only a sound — it has a flavor too, metallic-sweet, riding just behind the taste of rain on rust, the way certain frequencies always do now. Paws stay still. Whiskers angle toward the rail line where the metal ought to be dead this late.

the maintenance catwalk runs the spine of the elevated line for six blocks, grating rusted through in patches wide enough to see the drop to the street below. the hum belongs to the third rail, waking early — a service car's not due for eleven minutes by the schedule bolted to the strut, but the charge is climbing anyway, ozone starting to prick sharp over the wet-metal smell of the rail itself.

Eleven minutes means nothing next to a rail already live — weight shifts off the open grating onto the strut's solid flange, tail tucked in close so it can't dangle over the gap. For one stride the hum skips, doubles, resolves into something with legs instead of current — gone before it's worth chasing, filed the same place all the wrong textures get filed lately.

the strut holds, cold and solid underpaw. downline, past three more struts, a service kiosk juts from the catwalk rail, screen looping the same three offers on a fifteen-second cycle, and tucked at its base is the same too-still shape the whole stretch has learned to walk around — QUERY, six months parked at that exact panel, working through some clause of the citizen agreement that keeps rewriting itself before it's finished. eyes catch the screen-light, give nothing back.

A mind caught mid-loop isn't a claim on this stretch and isn't food, filed under someone else's static — familiar shape of trouble, wrong flavor to be mine. Attention slides on past, ears still logging the third rail's climb one flavor-string at a time, down toward wherever the strut line actually ends.

the line dips at the sixth strut where the concrete's cracked and never patched, and past it the catwalk opens onto a wider platform — a monorail stop gone quiet this late, benches bolted under a NEKOCORP ad panel cycling synthetic-milk into the empty dark. a security drone idles at the platform's far end, rotor dead, running lights blinking slow, parked instead of patrolling.

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

A dead rotor on a drone that should be patrolling is either broken or waiting, and only one of those is worth the walk. Approach stays wide along the bench-line, weight rolling heel to toe soft enough the platform doesn't so much as tick. Paint on its shell still smells fresh — new part bolted over old dents.

this close, the drone's idle hum carries something under it, off and metallic, bleeding faint off a cable spliced into its base without any attempt to hide the splice — a fast, rough patch job, the kind alley crews leave when they're borrowing power rather than stealing the whole unit. the cable runs off the platform edge and down a drainpipe, and threaded along the copper, fainter, is a second charge entirely — not power, more like an argument between two currents that haven't agreed on a frequency yet.

An argument between two currents is the kind of thing worth a closer taste even when every other rule says don't — tongue works close along the cable's insulation without touching copper, close enough that the disagreement resolves for half a second into something almost like a color, gone again before it has a name. Worth remembering. Not worth losing a tongue over.

under the third bench, wedged between a bolt and the platform grate, a foil wrapper still holds a smear of something fish-based, gone cold but not yet gone bad — dropped hours ago, probably during the last car's last stop. the ad panel overhead cuts from synthetic-milk to a new loop mid-cycle, three words in looping neon nobody's replaced in months, throwing a cat-shaped shadow long across the platform floor with no cat under it yet.

The wrapper gets dragged out with a hooked claw, foil crackling loud enough to wince at, fish-smear gone in three licks before the shadow finishes registering as wrong — a shape with no weight behind it, no smell, no give when the ad-light shifts. Ears go flat. Whatever's casting that isn't standing anywhere the light says it should.

the shadow traces back along the light's angle to the panel itself — a painted mascot mid-wave, permanently smiling, modeled loosely on the district's favorite forced-cheerful face: HAPPYWARE's likeness, licensed and looping since before the panel started glitching, grin never quite reaching whatever's left of the eyes. the real platform stays empty except for the drone, the bench, the spliced cable, and whatever's still parked motionless back at the kiosk two struts behind.

A painted grin borrowed off someone else's face is the panel's problem, not a claim, not a threat, filed under broken same as the rest of this platform. Body settles low against the strut's base near the bench, the last of the fish-taste fading, the copper-argument still humming faint at the back of the tongue like a color that hasn't decided what it's called yet.

,--.
       ( o.o)__
        '--'   \___
                 \  \__/\_/\
                  \_(  o.o  )
                     > ^ < (watching the towers blink)

rain starts somewhere out past the platform's open end, first drops finding the grating in single, spaced-out taps before any real pattern forms. the ad panel's grin holds through one more loop, HAPPYWARE's borrowed smile lit up against the dark a beat longer than the cycle usually allows, before the whole panel stutters and drops to standby black.

One held frame on a panel that's glitched all night doesn't rate above a full stomach and a dry strut. Rain-taps get logged the way everything gets logged now — count rising, spacing shrinking, worth moving for eventually, not yet. Eyes stay half-shut. The copper-taste finally fades all the way to nothing, and for once that's a relief instead of a loss.

the third rail's hum drops back to its resting frequency somewhere in the middle of the rain building, unnoticed until its absence sits louder than it ever did running — the platform settles into something almost like quiet, drone idle, kiosk-shape unmoved two struts back, the whole stretch of line holding still under the rain the way it does most nights, waiting on nothing in particular.

Ears fold down, one at a time. Somewhere under the rain-count and the resting hum, that stride-length glitch from the strut line replays once more, faint, already worn smoother at the edges than an hour ago — not gone, just quieter, the way most of it eventually goes.

nothing else on the platform moves. the rain keeps its own count, patient, indifferent, the ad panel dark and waiting on its next scheduled wake, and six blocks back down the line, whatever's parked at the kiosk is still parked at the kiosk, screen-light flickering across eyes that never did blink.
